name: Dynamic Buffer Management via CUDA Virtual Memory
aliases: Virtual Memory Management (VMM) for Dynamic Buffers
definition: A technique using CUDA's virtual memory management to store data in a single consecutive virtual address range that physically grows or shrinks, allowing dynamic resizing of splat buffers without copying data.
summary: Dynamic Buffer Management via CUDA Virtual Memory merges buffers by expanding existing virtual address ranges without allocating new memory or copying data, reducing overhead compared to standard allocation methods.
